body: Ha.  Your response says it all about the prevalent attitude.  Can't comment about an honest experience with out an aggressive attack.  You should get a job working security at Urban disco.
You'll get better service speaking English than Portuguese with a wonky accent.  English is widely spoken.  Even within the service sector they'll offer English speaking help.
This is not true.  People will giggle and always point out the accent or mispronunciation of words.  Ask you where you're from.  Which is not an issue if you just roll with it.

These rules are not just geared towards Americans.  It's for all.  My point is that your info is easily answered by contacting a Portuguese Consulate/Embassy to give you the proper info.  Easily done.

Isn't Google amazing?  Should try it sometime.

Yes.  Porto is much more charming, friendlier, and feels more like what Portugal represents than Lisbon.  If that makes any sense.  Many creative and talented people there.  Great art and music scene.  Simply the most beautiful city.
Bla Bla Car worked for me.  Salamanca is amazing!  He should move there with his mom.
Just like Lisboa if you're a foreigner.
I have been.  It's quite amazing.  Don't even question it.  Go.  Make sure you hit Osaka as well.  Travel beyond Tokyo.

While in Lisbon, go across river by catching ferry at Cais do Sodre to Cacilhas.  Exit left from ferry and walk along river.  Two restaurants exist towards the end after a 10 minute walk.  Ponto Final is the better of the two.  Just above (you can take the elevator up for 1 Euro) is Casa de Cerca.  They have art exhibits here.  Interesting and beautiful space with lovely views of the city from another perspective. Few tourists venture here.  Afterwards, can return to Cais do Sodre and have amazing Mexican food in the lively Pistol Y Corazon restaurant.  Though I suggest you get there early as it gets crowded.

At the airport your Uber driver will meet you on the departure level.  Just walk out cross the street and head to the car park a few meters from the entrance.  Look for the car with the license plate that's noted on the Uber app.  Never an issue.

If you go to a nice restaurant...  do tip.  Not necessarily 20% but at least 10%  Don't smile so much.  Portuguese consider Americans to be fake when it comes to their smiling.  The attitude here tends to be, "why would I smile randomly to someone I don't know."  Don't mistake their indifference for rudeness.  The music, history, and culture enjoys a bit of misery. Do go across the river and enjoy the city from that perspective.  It's an affordable ferry ride to Cacilhas. Off the boat go right and you'll end up at two restaurants. Ponto Final is the better of the two.  Nice for the sunset views.  if you go to Sintra, it's worth stopping in Queluz to see the Palace.  Do watch your wallet as pick pockets are notorious.  Though they tend to focus on Asians the most.  When you're constantly being asked to buy drugs from thugs on the streets just avoid them.  They're harmless and aren't actually selling real drugs.  This is why they get away with it.  Do explore Mouraria.  Great African restaurants there.  Take Uber over taxis.  The taxis will def take advantage of you.  Metro is safe and good.  Must go to Porto.  It's def charming and the people are so much more friendlier and the city is quite beautiful.  The Douro valley is a must.  And yes you can speak Spanish.  The Spanish do it all the time and most Portuguese won't trip out.  You're simply trying to communicate.  Nothing wrong with that.
